Historic Mujibnagar Day today
2026-04-17T02:54:47+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/historic-mujibnagar-day-today-4153506

Today is the historic Mujibnagar Day, the day Bangladesh’s first government took oath in 1971 amid the Liberation War.

On this day in 1971, senior Awami League leaders, who had formed the provisional government of independent Bangladesh a week earlier, assembled at Baidyanath Tala in Meherpur to take part in the oath-taking ceremony.

Around 10:00am, the leaders gathered at a mango orchard and took an oath to ensure equality, human dignity, and social justice for the people of Bangladesh.

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who was imprisoned in Pakistan, was declared the first President of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh. Syed Nazrul Islam was made vice-president and, in Sheikh Mujib’s absence, appointed acting president.

Bangladesh speaks to the world

Tajuddin Ahmad was sworn in as prime minister.

After the swearing-in, Syed Nazrul Islam, along with MAG Osmani, the newly appointed commander-in-chief of the Bangladesh Defence Forces, took the salute from a guard of honour, followed by an inspection.

The acting president raised the red, green, and yellow national flag amid thunderous applause. It was hoisted as the leaders and others present sang Amar Sonar Bangla in unison.

Baidyanath Tala was later renamed Mujibnagar.

On April 10, 1971, the Mujibnagar government was formed to lead the Liberation War and formally declare Bangladesh’s independence. Members of the National and Provincial Assemblies who were in India also constituted a constituent assembly.

The Proclamation of Independence was also made on this day. It served as the Constitution of Bangladesh from March 26, 1971, to December 16, 1972.
